messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: inference-prod GPU pool saturation detected. queue_depth: inference-worker routes > 120s for multiple customers. HPA not scaling (desired=4,max=4). metrics-adapter heartbeat missing. PagerDuty: paging infra-oncall. :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Paging infra-oncall -> @samir :ring:
infra-oncall (samir): Ack. I’m on it. Quick check: are customers seeing 502s or just high latency? :eyes:
support (alex): Customer reports elevated latencies and some throttled requests, no widespread 5xx. A few retries hitting rate limits.
ml-runtime (ellie): Queue length on gpu-worker pods jumped from ~50 to ~800 in the last 8m. Autoscale churned but HPA desired stayed at 4. suspect metrics lag or adapter failing to serve custom metrics.
sre-lead (mike): Can you paste HPA status + metrics-adapter logs?
ml-runtime (ellie): HPA status:

```
kubectl get hpa -n inference gpu-worker
NAME         REFERENCE            TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
gpu-worker   Deployment/gpu-worker  avgq/100   2         4         4          12h
```
Metrics adapter pods show CrashLoopBackOff in last 5m. logs contain repeated timeout fetching from Prometheus: "error querying prometheus: context deadline exceeded"
infra-oncall (samir): Thanks. Root cause likely metrics pipeline/backpressure. Immediate mitigation: 1) manual scale deployment to relieve queue 2) restart metrics-adapter to rehydrate metrics 3) enable temporary routing to dedicated pool if available. Doing step 1 now.
deploy-bot: Running command: `kubectl scale deployment/gpu-worker -n inference --replicas=8` :white_check_mark:
infra-oncall (samir): Scaling to 8 replicas. Monitor queue drain and token usage.
ml-runtime (ellie): Noted. Also we should raise HPA.maxReplicas so it can recover once adapter is back. current max=4. Propose bump to 50 temporarily.
sre-lead (mike): Agreed. I'll patch HPA to max 50 and apply a short cooldown. Doing patch now:

```
kubectl patch hpa gpu-worker -n inference -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":50}}'
```
apply: success. :thumbsup:
infra-oncall (samir): Restarting metrics-adapter to attempt backfill: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/metrics-adapter -n monitoring`
deploy-bot: rollout restart triggered for deployment/metrics-adapter :white_check_mark:
ml-runtime (ellie): Watching Prom scrape dashboard — prom shows scrape backlog and adapter queue spike. After restart adapter logs show successful connects and backfill starting. Metrics for avgq are now reporting. :eyes:
product-ops (karen): Heads-up: we have 3 paying customers on the critical SLA path that will see degraded latency until the queue drains. We may need to offer credits if >30m.
support (alex): Notifying account owners with current ETA for mitigation and recommending client retries with exponential backoff.
infra-oncall (samir): Observed queue length dropping from 800 -> 420 -> 200 over last 6m. Pod CPU on new replicas rising as work is consumed. No new significant 5xx.
ml-runtime (ellie): HPA controller now seeing metrics and should start scaling automatically. Keep manual scale until HPA upscales more gradually.
sre-lead (mike): Quick note: why did adapter timeout? Early signals: Prometheus scrape worker had overloaded disk IO and high retention compaction. Opening follow-up ticket. For live, we've restarted prom-scrape and metrics-adapter.
infra-oncall (samir): Handing off to next oncall in 15m. Current status: manual scale=8, HPA.max=50, metrics-adapter healthy, queue decreasing, critical customers notified. Escalation: if queue stops decreasing or 5xxs resume, page SRE lead.
product-ops (karen): Documenting customer impact: 3 customers had median latencies 3-6x baseline; no data loss; estimated restoration to normal in ~10-20m if drain continues.
support (alex): Log of outreach messages sent to affected accounts attached in case tracking required.
ml-runtime (ellie): Running two additional mitigations: 1) enable prefix-KV cache for hot requests to reduce work on backend, 2) temporarily reduce per-request max batch size to lower tail latency. Commands applied to config-service.
infra-oncall (samir): Next steps before handoff: monitor queue for steady decline (target <50), ensure HPA has transitioned to desired replicas < max, confirm no further prom scrape OOMs, and revert HPA.maxReplicas back to configured default once stable.
sre-lead (mike): Noted. I'll follow up with a postmortem starter and record timeline + root cause: prom IO spikes causing adapter timeouts -> delayed custom metrics -> HPA couldn't scale -> queue growth -> manual mitigations.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, partial recovery observed. Severity reduced to P2 pending full queue drain. :white_check_mark:
infra-oncall (samir): Handoff now to @mike for ongoing verification. I’m logging all commands in the runbook under incidents/3023456789. Leaving channel. :wave:
ml-runtime (ellie): Thanks all. Will monitor for next 30m and post final close.
support (alex): Customers still watching; will update if anything changes.
sre-lead (mike): Closing note at +25m: queue at 38, latencies back to baseline for most customers, metrics stable. Will follow up with RCA and remediation plan (prometheus retention tweak, adapter scaling, disk IO investigation).
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: queue drained, autoscale restored. Recording postmortem link when available. :tada:
